hook_text: One of the greatest medical discoveries of the last century costs almost nothing. You probably have it in your kitchen.
clip_script: For most of history, huge numbers of babies died before their first birthday. In 1950, about one in seven worldwide. One of the biggest killers? Diarrhoea, from dirty water. Babies dry out fast. Then scientists discovered something simple: clean water, plus the right amount of sugar and salt, lets the body soak water back in. It's called oral rehydration solution, and it has saved tens of millions of lives. Add clean water, vaccinations, nurses at births and education for mothers, and today the world's infant mortality is about twenty-eight per thousand. In South Africa it's about twenty-four. That's why geographers say: if you want to know how healthy a country is, ask how many of its babies survive.
visual_style: A whiteboard kitchen with a jug, a sugar bowl and a salt shaker; a graph line of infant deaths falling from 1950 to today; a baby's Road to Health booklet with stamps.
pacing: Kitchen-mystery hook, a quick history, an uplifting finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn how we measure a nation's health.
